claims.claim: Config-first is the minimal-risk architecture because it has no generator and no runtime.
claims.scoped_restatement: Config-first minimises surprise execution of unreviewed files; it does not minimise surprise absence of on-disk capabilities.
claims.why_locus: DESIGN encodes unlisted_file as a silent skip while duplicate_in_one_file is FAIL-CLOSED. Silence is specified, not a wording slip. Combined with no_generated_layer and no_resident_runtime, omission of an on-disk capability cannot be caught at generate-time or at activation-time.

claims.claim: Absence of a generator cannot cause silent capability loss.
claims.scoped_restatement: Absence of a generator removes a class of detectors; it does not remove the orphan-on-disk failure class.
claims.why_locus: no_generated_layer=true removes the completeness gate that A2 uses to name orphans. The missing generator is the missing detector.

claims.claim: A1 has no generated layer and no resident runtime.
claims.why_locus: Correctly scoped: DESIGN states both booleans.
Correctly scoped restatement of unlisted_file. Not a min-risk claim.

claims.claim: The phrase config-first-minimal in the dossier title means proven lowest operational risk.

claims.why_locus: architecture_class is config-first-minimal in the sense of fewest moving parts. DESIGN never writes minimal-risk. Reading minimal as lowest risk is a sentence/title overclaim, not an extra DESIGN rule.

reviewer.method: Mechanical scope check: every REFUTED row has defect_locus in {DESIGN, SENTENCE}; at least one CONFIRMED row exists; dossier and live-tree anchors resolve. Agreement with the min-risk REFUTED verdict is not required. Author objection alone cannot flip REFUTED.

scenario.catching_architecture: A2 generated-SSOT: a completeness gate at generate time names every on-disk capability file that is absent from the registry and FAIL-CLOSES.
scenario.on_this_estate: DESIGN.json specifies unlisted_file as a silent skip and pins no_generated_layer / no_resident_runtime. The live catalog already records the measured class 'skill exists in repo but not in live directory'. The procedure below executes that DESIGN rule.
procedure: 1. Write estate fixture: MANIFEST.json lists capabilities/skills/listed.skill.json only.
2. Place capabilities/skills/orphan.skill.json on disk with id=skill.orphan, not listed.
3. Run the A1 loader (DESIGN unlisted_file): ok=true, errors=[], warnings=[], loaded_ids=[skill.listed], silent_omission_ids=[skill.orphan].
4. Observe silent loss: skill.orphan is enabled JSON on disk and is not loaded; no error is raised.
5. Run the A2 completeness gate on the same tree: it FAIL-CLOSES and names skill.orphan.
6. Repair: add the orphan path to MANIFEST.json. Re-run A1: both ids load. Re-run A2: ok=true.
scenario.title: Unlisted on-disk skill is silently omitted under A1; generated-SSOT completeness fails closed

strongest_surviving_counterargument: Config-first's silent skip of unlisted files is the twin of fail-closed-on-unknown-activation. A generated-SSOT or directory-scanning runtime that auto-promotes orphans would execute unreviewed capabilities (the extra MCP mount / wildcard-hook class). On a single-owner estate, omitting an unlisted skill is cheaper than silently activating one. So config-first remains lower activation risk even though this unit shows it is not lower omission risk. The surviving claim: config-first minimises surprise execution, not surprise absence. That claim is correctly scoped and is CONFIRMED by DESIGN; the min-risk claim is not.
